name: UK inflation & rates
summary: Bank Rate 4% after 5 Nov rise; markets price about an 82% chance of a December rise; October CPI due 18 Nov
state: UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in September, inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band, and the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov. Deputy Governor Lombardelli said on 10 Nov a further near-term rise is likely (Pound Sterling Live). After September GDP beat forecasts, markets priced an 82% chance of a December rise on 13 Nov, up from 50% at the start of the week (MarketScreener). October CPI is published on 18 Nov; a print above 4% would cross the Alert line.
for_you: Higher Bank Rate feeds through to tracker and variable mortgages and new fixed deals, and to loan and card rates; savers tend to see better returns. Households renewing borrowing in the coming months are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Watch: CPI 3.5% within 2.5–4.0% band; BoE reversed course with a rise on 5 Nov

sources.title: Pound Sterling Live — Bank of England's Lombardelli Says December Rate Rise is in Play
MarketScreener (Dow Jones) — U.K. Gilt Yields Accelerate on Rate-Hike Expectations

why: UK inflation and the Bank Rate set mortgage, savings and business borrowing costs for the whole country.
drivers: Energy prices, wages, services inflation, sterling, global rates.

rubric.alert: CPI > 4.0%, or an emergency BoE move.
rubric.watch: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.
rubric.normal: CPI ≤ 2.5% and Bank of England moving gradually or on hold.
